body:
`insight:category-creation` · confidence: verified

Cases: Novo Nordisk (GLP-1 pioneer; Europe's most valuable company June 2024, then -73% to below pre-Wegovy levels by Feb 2026), Eli Lilly (fast follower with a better molecule; first $1tn drugmaker Nov 2025, ~63% of US branded obesity scripts), Monster (created a category and kept it), Celsius (new sub-category, 60x then -73%), Tesla (EVs; 35x then -73%), Nvidia (AI compute; see case_study:nvidia). Pattern: (1) the up-move begins when demand visibly exceeds supply (Wegovy shortages 2021-23, Model 3 waitlists, Pepsi DSD shelf space) — the signal is scarcity; (2) peak valuation tends to coincide with peak scarcity, exactly when competitors and capacity are arriving; (3) the winner is the player with the best head-to-head data/product and manufacturing/distribution scale (Lilly's SURPASS-2 and capacity spend; Monster's distribution system), not the first mover; (4) price normalisation (US government drug-price deals, compounding, EV price cuts) compresses margins at the same time as share loss. Early warning for the incumbent: a public head-to-head trial or benchmark that shows a superior rival, and its own next-gen product underwhelming (CagriSema Dec 2024). Lesson: in a new category, re-underwrite on competitive data every year; scarcity premiums are temporary.

- **Links:** `case_study:novo-nordisk-glp1-2016-2026`, `case_study:eli-lilly-2018-2025`, `case_study:nvidia`, `case_study:celsius-2020-2025`
- **Sources:** [1](https://finance.yahoo.com/news/novo-nordisks-475-billion-rise-165509914.html) · [2](https://finance.yahoo.com/news/lilly-becomes-first-drugmaker-join-145237391.html) · [3](https://bnnbloomberg.ca/business/company-news/2024/12/20/novo-nordisk-falls-most-on-record-after-new-weight-drug-disappoints)

body:
`theme:sector-it-services` · confidence: single-source · tickers: TCS, INFY, HCLTECH, WIPRO, TECHM, LTIM, PERSISTENT, COFORGE

**How it makes money:** Time-and-materials + fixed-price/managed services; arbitrage of offshore cost vs onshore billing.

**Metrics that matter:**
- Constant-currency revenue growth (QoQ, YoY)
- Deal TCV & net-new share; book-to-bill
- EBIT margin
- LTM attrition
- Utilisation (ex-trainees)
- Net headcount adds
- Top-5/10 client concentration
- Vertical exposure (BFSI)

**Value chain and where margins sit:** Global enterprise IT budget -> hyperscalers/SaaS vendors capture platform value -> SIs (Accenture) -> Indian IT (implementation, run, BPO) -> mid-tier/ER&D specialists. Highest margins in proprietary platforms/products and niche ER&D; lowest in commoditised app maintenance (most exposed to GenAI deflation).

**Cycle drivers:** US GDP/BFSI spend, tech-shift cycles, USD/INR, wage inflation and supply, visa policy, GenAI productivity pass-through to clients.

**Lead indicators (public India data):**
- Accenture quarterly results/bookings (reports ~3 weeks ahead)
- Gartner IT spending forecast
- US BLS computer systems design employment
- Naukri JobSpeak IT hiring index
- Mid-tier peers' commentary
- USD/INR

**What separated winners from losers:** Winners: early in each wave, high client mining (count of $100m clients rising), focused verticals, low attrition, disciplined pricing. Losers: legacy infra/app maintenance mix, management churn, expensive acquisitions to buy growth.

**Valuation ranges and peaks/troughs:** P/E 15–20x (2013–19), ~30–35x peak (Dec 2021), ~10–12x trough (2008–09). Nifty IT ~18.3x vs 7-yr median 27.1x (Jun 2026).

**Current state (Nov 2026):** Infosys Q2 FY27: $5.145 bn, +1.5% YoY CC (+1.2% QoQ), FY27 guidance cut to 1–2% (from 1.5–3%), op margin 21.0%, large-deal TCV $5.2 bn (62% net new), AI revenue +29% QoQ. TCS Q2 preview ~0.5–0.6% QoQ CC. Rupee growth (+10.7%) flatters reported numbers.

**Classic traps:**
- Mega-deal TCV that is mostly renewals or back-ended
- Rupee depreciation masquerading as growth
- Cheap vs history when terminal growth has structurally fallen (GenAI deflation)
- Margin 'beats' from lower subcontracting/hiring freezes that precede growth problems

body:
Stage 3 (signals), feeding stage 4 (deep dive) and 7 (scorekeeping): a nightly list of news, rating actions,
SEBI/RBI items and sector-policy headlines for the companies we cover, with "material" items ranked first.
It answers one question: *did something happen to a name we hold a view on that the filings may not show yet?*
(lessons L40 and L45: the land lease and the ethanol tender were both missing from the company's own documents).

Standard library plus the system `curl`. No logins, no API keys, no Claude. Runs by hand in a cloud session or
nightly on the Pi (`news` job, 22:30 IST, `deploy/pi/jobs.sh`). Research, not SEBI-registered advice: an item
means "read the source", not "trade".

```
python3 news.py                       # window --since 2d (default), whole watchlist + policy list
python3 news.py --since 7d            # also 36h or 2026-11-20
python3 news.py --tickers UTTAMSUGAR,US-KEX --sources google,ratings,sebi,rbi,policy
python3 news.py --selftest            # offline: fixture RSS/HTML, temp dir only (21 checks)
```

| File | What |
|---|---|
| `news.py` | fetch, match, rank, write |
| `watchlist.csv` | `ticker,name,sector,keywords,aliases,tier`. Seeded 25-Nov-2026 with the 8 live-dive tickers (`tier=live`) and every other memdb `paper-call` ticker (Indian and `US-` prefixed). `aliases` (`;`-separated) are extra search and match terms, `keywords` are company-specific watch words (tagged `watch_keyword`). |
| `policy.csv` | `sector,label,query`: Google News keyword queries per sector (sugar cane SAP/FRP, ethanol tender/OMC, microfinance, power tariff, USFDA actions, ...). A query runs only if a watchlist row has that sector. |

Outputs, in `$FEIN_DATA/news/` (default `~/fein-data/news/`):
- `YYYY-MM-DD.csv`: `date, ticker, source, headline, url, matched_rule`. `date` is the publish time (IST). The file is
  named for the run date (IST), so a run after midnight writes the next day's file.
- `YYYY-MM-DD.md`: four sections (material with the company named in the headline; material keyword, but the headline
  does not name the company; policy watch; other company news, at most 4 per ticker) plus a per-source status table and
  the list of sources that are never automated.
- `news.sqlite`: `seen` (dedup keys), `items` (every item reported, with rules) and `runs` (per-source counts).
  **Each item is reported once**: on the run that first sees it. Dedup keys are the canonical URL and the
  normalised headline plus ticker. A story found by two queries in one run is merged, and its tickers and rules are combined.
- Log: `$FEIN_DATA/logs/news.log`.

data.section: L12 (2026-11-20) — Our own checklist has measurable false alarms

title: lessons › L12 (2026-11-20) — Our own checklist has measurable false alarms

body:
- **History series:** World Bank monthly average gold price (USD/oz). Two start dates reported: **1968-04** (two-tier
  market; free price exists) and **1975-01** (US citizens may own gold; the market is broad). INR series = USD × EXINUS
  monthly (1973→; INR results start 1975-01).
- **Peak / drawdown episode:** running all-time high (ATH) of the monthly series. An episode starts at an ATH month and
  counts if the price later falls **≥20% below that ATH** before a new ATH. Depth = trough/peak − 1; fall duration =
  peak → trough months; **recovery = months from peak until the series first closes ≥ the old peak** (nominal). Open
  episodes are reported as open with duration so far. A 15% threshold is reported as a sensitivity only.
- **Real recovery** (sensitivity): same, deflated by US CPI.
- **Run-up (Q2):** ratio of peak to the minimum of the prior 36 months. "Big run-up" = ≥2.5× in ≤36 months. Also report
  the continuous relationship (run-up ratio vs depth and vs recovery months) across all episodes.
- **Fed regime (Q3):** at each month, 6-month change in FEDFUNDS: > +0.25pp = **hiking**, < −0.25pp = **cutting**, else
  **hold**. Real-yield level = DFII10 monthly average (2003→), proxy before (GS10 − CPI y/y). Real-yield change = 12-month
  change. For each episode: regime at the peak and during the fall; real-yield level and change over the fall; regime
  when recovery started (trough month).
- **Q4 cushion:** for each USD episode, INR return over the same peak→trough months, and the INR-series own episodes.
  Cushion = INR return − USD return (pp). Report how often INR depreciated during USD falls.
- **Q5 forecasts:** LBMA annual precious-metals forecast survey (published each January: consensus average-price
  forecast for the year) where the public pages give it; compare with actual annual average (World Bank). Benchmark =
  random walk (the December average before the forecast). Informative only if consensus mean absolute % error is lower
  than the random walk's in a majority of years AND on average. Bank year-end targets: list published 2025–26 targets with
  dates and sources and how they moved; no score unless ≥8 dated target/outcome pairs exist. "Buy zone below
  $3,600/$3,500" claim: find who said it, when, where; a "floor" counts as evidenced only by a dated, attributable flow
  number (e.g., WGC central-bank tonnes, ETF tonnes) at those prices, not by a commentator's sentence.
